title: Auto Loans: Closed Paying Account as a Bank Error on Returned Payments
content:
When an Auto Loans payment comes back unpaid, whether PCB is at fault depends on the kind of payment and on the state of the account it was drawn on. This note gives the test for returned payments.

## Rule

PCB error is established when the returned payment was an autopay debit and the checking account debited has, in the borrower's checking records, a closing date earlier than the date the debit posted.

PCB error is not established when any of the following is so:

- the payment that came back had been made some other way than by autopay debit;
- the debited account had not yet closed on the posting date, its closing date being that same day or a later one;
- the debited account shows no closing date at all.

The closing date is read from the checking records of the account that the payment was drawn on.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical debit posted 15 March 2031)

| Payment kind | Closing date of the paying account | PCB error |
|---|---|---|
| autopay debit | 14 March 2031 | yes |
| autopay debit | 15 March 2031 | no, the account was still open that day |
| autopay debit | none recorded | no |
| payment made by another method | 1 January 2031 | no, not an autopay debit |
